implementation_notes: NSCache is Foundation's thread-safe cache: object(forKey:) and setObject(_:forKey:cost:) store transient objects, entries are evicted automatically under memory pressure, and the instance can be used from several threads without extra locking, which is why it replaces a hand-written dictionary plus lock. The application still owns the protocol - a miss loads from the source of truth and sets the object with a cost and, for TTL, a deadline wrapper, while a write removes the key after the store commit. NSCache is per process and may drop entries at any time, so a shared tier still needs a client such as a Redis package.
pitfalls: NSCache has no TTL and may evict at any moment (even while a caller holds the returned object), so presence in the cache must never be treated as proof the value exists.
Keys are not copied and must be objects (KeyType: AnyObject); mutating a key after insertion makes the entry unreachable.
The cache retains its values strongly, so large or sensitive objects stay in memory until eviction - use NSDiscardableContent or do not cache them.

variants.name: actor with a Task-valued in-flight map (Swift concurrency)
variants.idiom_name: actor holding [Key: Task<Value, Error>] with deduplicated loads
variants.implementation_notes: Swift concurrency gives a lock-free structure for the same protocol: an actor serializes access to its state (Apple documents actors as running tasks on a serial executor), and storing the in-flight load as a Task rather than the value lets concurrent callers await the same source-of-truth read, which is the actor-world single-flight. Entries carry a deadline for TTL, invalidation removes the key after the store write, and the actor replaces the mutex; the cost is that no heavy or blocking work may run inside the actor.
pitfalls: Values that cross the actor boundary must be Sendable; storing a non-Sendable reference type compiles under leniency and races at runtime.
A failed in-flight Task must be removed from the map, or every later caller awaits the cached failure.
Long blocking loads inside the actor serialize all other cache access; run the I/O outside and keep only the bookkeeping inside.
